analysis:
Both supplied units are base-side text of docs/architecture/cache-aware-routing.md (lines 1-910). No patch hunks or head text were supplied, so the PR's actual changes are not visible. Coverage is limited; I did not infer that the change is safe. I report no findings.

The base text describes these security-relevant controls:
- Cache routing is default-off and flag-gated.
- Only protocol-v2 exact-token proofs count. The provider recomputes the token-chain anchor.
- The cache scope is a coordinator HMAC over authenticated account, model build, aggregate hash, prompt contract and block-hash version. It never comes from caller prompt_cache_key or user fields (lines 211-218).
- Per-attempt ownership is revalidated at writer dequeue (lines 242-258).
- Proof-mismatch fences run 60s to 10min (lines 325-339).
- Holder, attempt and byte caps apply (lines 450-560).
- Persistence is write-behind and SSD-only, with a delete-overflow reset (lines 562-664).
- The status API is aggregate-only.
- Selection prices a proven hit as an advisory estimate and does not authorize anything.

Relevant threats are T-041 (cross-tenant prefix cache and TTFT oracle, SEC-035 accepted), T-003 and T-007. The 30-minute SSD TTL and authenticated account scoping are baselines in T-041.

The next pass should check any head-side change for these regressions:
- Cache scope derived from caller fields.
- A TTL above 30 minutes.
- Weakened account isolation.
- Holders created without authenticated receipts.
- Status fields that leak model, provider or account identifiers.
- Docs claiming deployed or measured behavior that the code does not support.

T-041's detection_hint treats TTL and gate changes as needing a fresh SEC-035 sign-off.
